cards.front: Strategy: draw it
cards.back: Make a quick picture or bar model. It helps you see the numbers in the story.
cards.say: Strategy: draw it. Make a quick picture or bar model. It helps you see the numbers in the story.

cards.front: Strategy: find a pattern
cards.back: Look for the rule that repeats or grows, then use it to find what comes next.
cards.say: Strategy: find a pattern. Look for the rule that repeats or grows, then use it to find what comes next.

cards.front: Strategy: work backwards
cards.back: Start with the end result and undo each step in reverse order.
cards.say: Strategy: work backwards. Start with the end result and undo each step in reverse order.

cards.front: Strategy: make an organised list
cards.back: List all the options in a clear order so you do not miss any or count any twice.
cards.say: Strategy: make an organised list. List all the options in a clear order so you do not miss any or count any twice.

cards.front: Strategy: guess, check and improve
cards.back: Try an answer, check it, and use what you learn to make a better guess.
cards.say: Strategy: guess, check and improve. Try an answer, check it, and use what you learn to make a better guess.

cards.front: Strategy: use the clues one at a time
cards.back: Cross out numbers that do not fit each clue until only one is left.
cards.say: Strategy: use the clues one at a time. Cross out numbers that do not fit each clue until only one is left.

cards.front: What is a bar model?
cards.back: A drawing of bars that shows the parts and the whole of a story problem.
cards.say: What is a bar model? A drawing of bars that shows the parts and the whole of a story problem.

cards.back: 15. Add 3 each time.
cards.say: Pattern: three, six, nine, twelve, what comes next? Fifteen. Add three each time.

cards.front: Pattern: 1, 2, 4, 8, ?
cards.back: 16. Each number is double the one before.
cards.say: Pattern: one, two, four, eight, what comes next? Sixteen. Each number is double the one before.

cards.back: 8. Take away 3 each time.
cards.say: Pattern: twenty, seventeen, fourteen, eleven, what comes next? Eight. Take away three each time.

cards.back: 3. The pattern 1, 2, 3 repeats.
cards.say: Pattern: one, two, three, one, two, three, one, two, what comes next? Three. The pattern one, two, three repeats.

cards.front: I think of a number, double it and add 3. I get 11. What was my number?
cards.back: 4. Work backwards: 11 take away 3 is 8, and half of 8 is 4.
cards.say: I think of a number, double it and add three. I get eleven. What was my number? Four. Work backwards: eleven take away three is eight, and half of eight is four.

cards.front: I think of a number, halve it and add 5. I get 15. What was my number?
cards.back: 20. Work backwards: 15 take away 5 is 10, and double 10 is 20.
cards.say: I think of a number, halve it and add five. I get fifteen. What was my number? Twenty. Work backwards: fifteen take away five is ten, and double ten is twenty.

cards.front: Sam had some marbles. He lost 6, then won 4, and now has 15. How many did he start with?
cards.back: 17. Work backwards: 15 take away 4 is 11, then 11 + 6 = 17.
cards.say: Sam had some marbles. He lost six, then won four, and now has fifteen. How many did he start with? Seventeen. Work backwards: fifteen take away four is eleven, then eleven plus six equals seventeen.

cards.front: There are 20 apples. 12 are red and the rest are green. How many are green? Use a bar.
cards.back: 8 green apples. 20 take away 12 is 8.
cards.say: There are twenty apples. Twelve are red and the rest are green. How many are green? Eight green apples. Twenty take away twelve is eight.

cards.front: Ali and Bo have 14 stickers together. Ali has 4 more than Bo. How many does each have?
cards.back: Bo has 5 and Ali has 9. 5 + 9 = 14 and 9 is 4 more than 5.
cards.say: Ali and Bo have fourteen stickers together. Ali has four more than Bo. How many does each have? Bo has five and Ali has nine. Five plus nine equals fourteen and nine is four more than five.

cards.front: 4 hens and 3 cows. How many legs altogether?
cards.say: Four hens and three cows. How many legs altogether? Twenty legs. Hens: four times two equals eight. Cows: three times four equals twelve. Eight plus twelve equals twenty.

cards.front: A shop has 2 flavours of ice cream and 3 toppings. How many different choices?
cards.back: 6 choices. List: each flavour with each topping, 3 + 3 = 6.
cards.say: A shop has two flavours of ice cream and three toppings. How many different choices? Six choices. List each flavour with each topping, three plus three equals six.

cards.front: I am a 2-digit number. My digits add to 6 and my tens digit is double my ones digit. Who am I?
cards.back: 42. 4 + 2 = 6 and 4 is double 2.
cards.say: I am a two-digit number. My digits add to six and my tens digit is double my ones digit. Who am I? Forty-two. Four plus two equals six and four is double two.

cards.front: Find the odd one out: 10, 20, 35, 40
cards.back: 35. The others are in the 10 times table.
cards.say: Find the odd one out: ten, twenty, thirty-five, forty. Thirty-five. The others are in the ten times table.

cards.front: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 and D = 4, what is the number code for BAD?
cards.say: If A equals one, B equals two, C equals three and D equals four, what is the number code for BAD? Two, one, four.

cards.front: Which 3 coins make Rp700? Use Rp500, Rp200 and Rp100 coins.
cards.say: Which three coins make seven hundred rupiah? Use five hundred, two hundred and one hundred rupiah coins. Five hundred plus one hundred plus one hundred equals seven hundred rupiah.

cards.front: 3 friends each shake hands once with each other. How many handshakes?
cards.back: 3. A with B, A with C, B with C.
cards.say: Three friends each shake hands once with each other. How many handshakes? Three. A with B, A with C, B with C.

cards.front: Estimate 29 + 41. Is the answer closer to 50 or 70?
cards.back: 70. 29 is about 30 and 41 is about 40, and 30 + 40 = 70.
cards.say: Estimate twenty-nine plus forty-one. Is the answer closer to fifty or seventy? Seventy. Twenty-nine is about thirty and forty-one is about forty, and thirty plus forty equals seventy.

cards.front: Why should you check your answer?
cards.back: To catch mistakes. Use the opposite sum or ask if the answer is sensible.
cards.say: Why should you check your answer? To catch mistakes. Use the opposite sum or ask if the answer is sensible.
